name: Black Bird, at the gathering of August 1812
head: blackbird
review_note: review_required: a Potawatomi person of the gathering at Chicago in August 1812, the eve of the battle in which the garrison and its families were attacked. The card states only what the named sources say, says where a story is Kinzie family tradition rather than a contemporary account, and stages no speech or ceremony.

present_on_scene_date.note: Each person's own card says how their presence on 14 August is known.

associated_with.note: No source places his lodge in the camp; the card is put at one of the camp's grounds on the creek (the 1812 camp records) so it can be found, a reconstructed choice (liberty L-1812-people-3461).

not_in_this_household.note: No source names his family or places his lodge in the camp.

persons.name: Black Bird

present_on_scene_date.note: Presence on the afternoon of 14 August 1812, read from the evidence below; no source takes a roll call that afternoon.

also_written: Siggenauk (Encyclopedia of Chicago identifies the 1812 Blackbird with Siggenauk)
persons.note: War leader of the attack; received Heald's surrender. Potawatomi; in May 1812 of Pepper's band at the Au Sable (Andreas, OCR); Encyclopedia of Chicago calls Siggenauk 'a leader from Chicago'. Leader on the 15th (Heald, contemporary). Nothing places him on the 14th directly. 15 and 16 August: Met Heald with the interpreter and requested surrender, promising to spare prisoners (Heald 1812; Helm 1814). Afterwards: Not established here.
